$comment: Tips shown by both IDEs. VS Code: the Get Started walkthrough (clients/vscode/scripts/copy-assets.js writes the steps into package.json). IntelliJ: Tip of the Day and the plugin's Tips dialog (Gradle turns each tip into tips/AzureTemplates_<id>.html; plugin.xml lists them, TipsParityTest checks it). Text supports **bold**, *italic*, `code` and [links](https://…). In `intellij`, {shortcut:ActionId} becomes that action's shortcut. `example` is shown as a code block next to the tip, highlighted as `exampleLanguage`.

tips.title: Will this pipeline run?
tips.vscode: Every pipeline shows a verdict above its first line, covering the pipeline and every template it reaches. Click it to list the problems. The **Pipelines** view lists every pipeline in the workspace, failing first.
tips.intellij: Every pipeline shows a verdict above its first line, covering the pipeline and every template it reaches. Click it to list the problems. The **Pipelines** tab of the Azure Templates tool window lists every pipeline in the project, failing first.
tips.example:
✗ Will fail when queued: 2 errors, 1 warning
trigger:
  branches:
    include: [main]

tips.title: What did my changes break?
tips.vscode: When many pipelines already fail, click **Show My Changes** in the title of the **Pipelines** view. It compares your work with where it started (where your branch split from the branch it came from, committed or not): the files you changed, the problems they added and fixed, and the pipelines they reach, with the total underneath. The **Diagnostics** view follows the same switch. Click the *Since* row to compare with another branch or with your last commit. Turn on `changes.dimExistingProblems` to show the older problems as information in the Problems panel.
tips.intellij: When many pipelines already fail, turn on **Only My Changes** in the toolbar of the **Pipelines** tab. It compares your work with where it started (where your branch split from the branch it came from, committed or not): the files you changed, the problems they added and fixed, and the pipelines they reach, with the total underneath. The **Diagnostics** tab follows the same switch. *Compare My Changes With…* picks another branch or your last commit. In Settings, *Show problems that were already there before my changes as information* quiets the Problems tool window.
tips.example:
Since origin/main @ 3f2a1c4    2 commits + uncommitted
Files changed (1)
  templates/run-tests.yml    modified · 3 pipelines use it
1 file changed · 3 pipelines affected · 4 new errors
  azure-pipelines.yml    +2 new · 1 already there

tips.title: See a template's parameters
tips.vscode: Hover a `template:` line to see the template's parameters, with their types, defaults and allowed values. Required ones are highlighted. Ctrl/Cmd+click opens the template.
tips.intellij: Put the caret on a `template:` line and press {shortcut:QuickJavaDoc} (Quick Documentation) to see the template's parameters, with their types, defaults and allowed values. Ctrl/Cmd+click, or the gutter icon, opens the template.
tips.example:
- template: build.yml        ← hover here
  parameters:
    configuration: Release

tips.title: Complete a template call in one go
tips.vscode: Completing a template path also inserts a `parameters:` block with the template's required parameters. Press Tab to move between the values.
tips.intellij: Completing a template path also inserts a `parameters:` block with the template's required parameters. Press Tab to move between the values. Turn it off in *Settings | Tools | Azure Templates Navigator*.

tips.title: Fix template calls from the problem
tips.vscode: Missing required parameters, misspelled names ("did you mean"), values outside `values:` and missing templates are reported as you type. Most of them have a quick fix: press Ctrl+. (Cmd+. on macOS) on the problem.
tips.intellij: Missing required parameters, misspelled names ("did you mean"), values outside `values:` and missing templates are reported as you type. Most of them have a quick fix: press {shortcut:ShowIntentionActions} on the problem.
tips.example:
- template: build.yml
  parameters:
    confguration: Release   ← Unknown parameter 'confguration'. Did you mean 'configuration'?

tips.title: Keep a known problem quiet
tips.vscode: Some problems are on purpose, like a parameter kept only so older callers don't break. Press Ctrl+. (Cmd+. on macOS) on the problem and pick **Ignore '…' on this line** or **Ignore '…' in this file**. It writes an `# atn-ignore` comment that names the problem's code, so nothing else is hidden, and the pipeline's verdict stops counting it. Delete the comment to see the problem again.
tips.intellij: Some problems are on purpose, like a parameter kept only so older callers don't break. Press {shortcut:ShowIntentionActions} on the problem and pick **Ignore '…' on this line** or **Ignore '…' in this file**. It writes an `# atn-ignore` comment that names the problem's code, so nothing else is hidden, and the pipeline's verdict stops counting it. Delete the comment to see the problem again.
tips.example:
# atn-ignore-file undeclared-param
parameters:
# kept so v2 callers don't break
# atn-ignore unused-param
- name: legacyAgentPool
  type: string
  default: ''

tips.title: Who uses this template?
tips.vscode: Before you change a template, check who calls it. The "N usages" lens above the template lists its call sites, and Find All References (Shift+Alt+F12) works on templates and on their parameters.
tips.intellij: Before you change a template, check who calls it. The "N usages" hint above the template lists its call sites, and Find Usages ({shortcut:FindUsages}) works on templates and on their parameters. {shortcut:ShowUsages} shows them in a popup.
tips.example:
3 usages
parameters:
  - name: configuration
    type: string

tips.title: Follow the chain from pipeline to template
tips.vscode: On a template, *Show Call Hierarchy* (Shift+Alt+H) lists the templates that call it, the pipelines that call those, and so on up to every pipeline that reaches it. Its toggle shows the other direction: everything a pipeline calls.
tips.intellij: On a template, Call Hierarchy ({shortcut:CallHierarchy}) lists the templates that call it, the pipelines that call those, and so on up to every pipeline that reaches it. Its toolbar shows the other direction: everything a pipeline calls.

tips.title: See how pipelines and templates connect
tips.vscode: The **Template Graph** draws the current file with its callers and callees, or the whole workspace. Bigger nodes are used more. Click a node to light up everything that reaches it and everything it calls, and filter to problems, kinds or repositories.
tips.intellij: The **Graph** tab of the Azure Templates tool window draws the current file with its callers and callees, or the whole project. Bigger nodes are used more. Click a node to light up everything that reaches it and everything it calls, and use *Only Problems* or *Filter* in its toolbar.

tips.title: Templates from other repositories
tips.vscode: `template: x.yml@templates` works like a local template: the repository is downloaded into a shared cache with your normal git credentials, and refreshed in the background. The **Repositories** view shows each one's state and the templates you use from it.
tips.intellij: `template: x.yml@templates` works like a local template: the repository is downloaded into a shared cache with your normal git credentials, and refreshed in the background. The **Repositories** tab shows each one's state and the templates you use from it.
tips.example:
resources:
  repositories:
    - repository: templates
      type: github
      name: my-org/pipeline-templates
steps:
  - template: build.yml@templates

tips.title: When a repository can't be found
tips.vscode: Most repositories need no setup. If one shows as failed or unconfigured in the **Repositories** view, or your templates live in a folder rather than their own repository, commit `.azure-templates-navigator.json` at the repository root. `urls` pins an alias's clone URL. `localPaths` points an alias at a folder, which is then read as is, with no download. Everyone gets the same mapping, in VS Code, IntelliJ and the `atn` CLI.
tips.intellij: Most repositories need no setup. If one shows as failed or unconfigured in the **Repositories** tab, or your templates live in a folder rather than their own repository, commit `.azure-templates-navigator.json` at the repository root. `urls` pins an alias's clone URL. `localPaths` points an alias at a folder, which is then read as is, with no download. Everyone gets the same mapping, in IntelliJ, VS Code and the `atn` CLI.

tips.title: Stats for template owners
tips.vscode: The **Stats** view shows problems by type, the most used and most mis-called templates, templates nothing references, and counts per repository. Click a row to open the file, or *Show in Graph* to see it in context.
tips.intellij: The **Stats** tab shows problems by type, the most used and most mis-called templates, templates nothing references, and counts per repository. Click a row to open the file, or *Show in Graph* to see it in context.
tips.example:
Most used
  build.yml           42 calls · 17 pipelines
  deploy.yml          31 calls · 12 pipelines
Not referenced in this workspace
  legacy/old-build.yml

tips.title: The same checks in CI
tips.vscode: The `atn` binary behind this extension also runs in a terminal or a pipeline: `atn check` prints every pipeline's verdict and exits with 1 on errors. `--format azure` turns the problems into annotations on the run. See the [CLI documentation](https://github.com/qSharpy/azure-templates-navigator#cli).
tips.intellij: The `atn` binary behind this plugin also runs in a terminal or a pipeline: `atn check` prints every pipeline's verdict and exits with 1 on errors. `--format azure` turns the problems into annotations on the run. See the [CLI documentation](https://github.com/qSharpy/azure-templates-navigator#cli).
tips.example:
$ atn check
Pipelines:
  azure-pipelines.yml     ✗ Will fail when queued: 1 error
  pipelines/nightly.yml   ✓ No problems found before running
